business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial Mail Receiving Agency (CMRA) and Digital Scanning

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States-Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA, in force 31 October 2012)
United Kingdom-Panama Double Taxation Agreement (in force 2020)
Kingdom of the Netherlands-Panama Double Taxation Convention (in force 2001)
Kingdom of Spain-Panama Double Taxation Agreement (in force 2012)
Grand Duchy of Luxembourg-Panama Double Taxation Agreement (in force 2011)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (Panama AML/CFT framework, UAF powers, CDD obligations), as amended; Decreto Ejecutivo No. 129 de 21 de octubre de 2020 and DGI implementing resolutions creating the mandatory Registro de Beneficiarios Finales; Ley No. 254 de 2023 (final beneficial owner registry reform and enforcement enhancement); Ley No. 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927 (Sociedad Anónima regime); UAF Resolution No. 001-2021 (PEP, sanction and CDD/EDD implementation rules).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport page(s) of each direct shareholder, UBO, director and officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of each natural person's country of origin (national passport office or civil registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization at the Panamanian Embassy if country is not an Apostille party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Panamanian resident agent and corporate counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin, plus further notarization before a Panamanian Notary of the Circuito
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille in country of origin plus Panamanian notarial protocol

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and/or Certificate of Incumbency for each corporate shareholder or corporate director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry and corporate secretary of the jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds certificate for each UBO making an initial contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Hague Apostille (or consular legalization), supplemented by direct bank-to-resident-agent verification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of physical residential address of each UBO (current utility bill or notarial affidavit of residence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or notary public of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Hague Apostille (or consular legalization)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based CDD/EDD screening of all UBOs, shareholders, directors and officers against the Panamanian UAF high-risk list, OFAC SDN/SSI, UNSC Consolidated List, EU consolidated financial sanctions and INTERPOL Red Notices; PEP identification via self-declaration, public-office and electoral databases, and adverse-media checks; any PEP, family member or close associate triggers enhanced due diligence and prior senior-management approval. Ley 23 de 2015, as amended, and UAF Resolution 001-2021 govern the protocol and require that all screening and CDD files be retained for a minimum of five (5) years from termination of the relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Personas Jurídicas (online "Vista" name search and name-certificate issuance service, www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be composed in the Latin alphabet; Spanish-language denominations are preferred, and foreign words must be transliterated phonetically into Spanish script. The name of a Sociedad Anónima must conclude with the distinguishing expression "Sociedad Anónima" or the abbreviation "S.A."; identical, confusingly similar, or phonetically equivalent names already recorded in the Registry are prohibited.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco, Banca, Financiera (requires prior authorization from the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá)
Seguros, Reaseguros (requires prior authorization from the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros)
Trust, Fiduciario, Fideicomiso (requires prior authorization from the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá)
Bolsa de Valores, Casa de Valores (requires prior authorization from the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores)
Ministerio, Gobierno, Estado, Presidencia, Nacional, Policía Nacional, Universidad, Cruz Roja (state or institutional connotations prohibited without ministerial consent)
Oficina de Abogados, Notaría, Despacho Jurídico (reserved for licensed Panamanian lawyers and prohibited in a commercial corporate name unless the entity is properly licensed)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant through its attorney or resident agent may file a written "recurso de reconsideración" before the Director General of the Registro Público within five (5) business days of notification; a further "recurso de apelación" may be brought to the Junta Directiva of the Registry, and final administrative relief lies via a "demanda contencioso-administrativa" before the Sala Tercera de la Corte Suprema de Justicia within two (2) months of the final administrative decision. For expedited processing, an alternative name may be resubmitted without exhausting the appeal remedy.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the CMRA mail-scanning business purpose, subject to conditionality: the company must maintain a genuine physical commercial address in Panama for licensing, invoicing and client-service premises, and each client relationship must be supported by a written virtual-office agreement with verified customer identification pursuant to CDD obligations. A PO Box or non-physical address is not acceptable for statutory registered-office purposes, for resident-agent designation, or for bank-account domiciliation under FATF/BCP standards.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate: approximately 20% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection for a newly incorporated CMRA-type entity in Panama, driven by DGI tax audits, municipal Aviso de Operación licensing inspections, and UAF AML/CFT site visits; the probability rises to approximately 35% where the mail-scanning model serves predominantly non-resident clients or processes high transaction volumes.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and issuance of the name certificate (Certificado de Nombre) by the Registro Público de Panamá
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official statutory tariff (arancel) of the Registro Público

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation (Escritura Pública de Constitución) and initial corporate minutes before a Panamanian Notary of the Circuito
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market notarial fee scale (approx. USD 150-300 per protocol)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial registration and filing of the incorporation deed with the Legal Entities Section of the Registro Público de Panamá
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff dependent on authorized capital; prevailing benchmark USD 150-350

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille certificates for the required notarization bundle (passport copies, POA, good-standing certificate, bank reference, proof of address)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of each country of origin (e.g., Ministry of Foreign Affairs or Secretary of State)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official statutory apostille fee per document (USD 5-30 counterpart fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial one-year resident agent and registered office fee (agente residente) for the Sociedad Anónima
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian resident agent firm (regulated under Ley 32 de 1927 and Registro Público rules)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for standard S.A. maintenance (USD 300-800 per annum)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional legal fees for pre-incorporation structuring, UBO identification, AML/CFT file assembly and submission of the name clearance dossier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed-fee benchmark (USD 600-1,200 inclusive of all related filings)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO initial registration filing with the Dirección General de Ingresos (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) - government processing and professional filing component
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Nominal governmental processing fee plus professional submission fee; limited published statutory tariff (USD 0-50)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927 (Panama Corporations Law) as amended; Disposiciones Generales of the Registro Público de Panamá; Decreto de Gabinete No. 4 de 1999 regarding the Public Registry; additional electronic-document support under Ley 5 de 2016
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección Mercantil (Public Registry of Panama, Mercantile Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation) containing the Articles of Incorporation (Pacto Social / Estatutos), filed with the Public Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed capital of USD 10,000.00; at least 3% (USD 300.00) must be paid up in cash or property at formation. No escrow account is mandated by law; payment is evidenced by the notarized capital subscription statement recorded in the Public Deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by unanimous consent of the subscribing directors of [Company Name], S.A., held on this [date] at the registered agent's offices: First, the founder's subscription of 100 fully paid registered shares at USD 100.00 par value each, totaling USD 10,000.00, is hereby approved and recorded in the Share Register. Second, the registered office at [registered agent address], Panama, is adopted and ratified as the statutory domicile. Third, [President Name], [Secretary Name], and [Treasurer Name] are appointed President, Secretary, and Treasurer, respectively, each for a one-year term. Fourth, the President is authorized to open bank accounts and execute all statutory filings, and the Resident Agent, [Agent Name], is ratified. Passed unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Registered-Agent Designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — online via SAG-RP (Sistema de Atención General del Registro Público)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the corporate name reservation application through the licensed Panamanian attorney or registered agent, providing three preferred names with the 'S.A.' or 'Corp.' suffix. The application must verify that the requested name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity and does not contain protected terms (banking, insurance, governmental). Upon approval, obtain the official reservation certificate and simultaneously confirm the resident-agent acceptance letter, as the registered agent is mandatory for every Panama S.A.
required_dossiers: Notarized power of attorney (Poder) granted to the Panamanian attorney or resident agent
Name reservation application form (Solicitud de Reserva de Nombre)
Certified copy of passport or national ID of each incorporador/subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar, immediately refile with alternative names within 48 hours; a reconsideration petition may be filed with the Registro Público under applicable registral regulations (Disposición Registral correspondiente) without additional government charges.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation (Escritura Pública)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of Panama (Notario Público) acting with the resident agent or licensed attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Public Deed containing the articles of incorporation: corporate name, domicile, purpose (including virtual office, CMRA mail receipt and digital scanning under ISIC 8299), capital structure, share classes, duration, directors, and the registered agent. Execute the deed before a Panamanian notary physically or by electronic signature under Ley 5 de 2016. Obtain certified first copy (primer testimonio) and pay applicable documentary stamps (timbre) at this stage.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate issued by the Registro Público
Draft Articles of Incorporation / Estatutos
Identity documents of all incorporators
Registered agent acceptance letter
Power of attorney if execution is made by attorney-in-fact
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies omissions, execute a corrective amendment (reforma o ampliación) to the deed prior to registry filing; in the alternative, re-execute the deed in clean form with all required clauses incorporated; no registry query exists at this pre-filing stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Corporation with the Public Registry (Folio Electrónico)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the certified first copy (primer testimonio) of the Public Deed together with the registry cover sheet and fee payment at the Mercantile Section of the Public Registry. The titles officer reviews legality, capital adequacy, and due taxation. After approval, the corporation is registered and a Folio Electrónico is opened; a Certificate of Registration (Certificado de Registro) is then issued as official evidence of existence.
required_dossiers: Certified first copy of the Public Deed of Incorporation
Registered agent acceptance and confirmation letter
Tax stamp (timbre) payment receipt
Registral fee payment receipt
SAG-RP filing cover page
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the titles officer issues a defect notice (calificación adversa), the attorney files a written cure (escrito de saneamiento) within the statutory term; any omitted clause is corrected through a notarial amendment deed re-submitted for registration. An appeal to the Superior Title Tribunal is available if the defect notice is contested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration — RUC and Electronic Tax Account (e-Tax)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (portal: www.dgi.gob.pa)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the newly formed S.A. in the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) through the DGI virtual office (SIF — Sistema de Información Fiscal). Provide the corporate Folio number, Public Deed metadata, representative identity, and proof of registered address. Upon registration, the company obtains its RUC number, activates the e-Tax electronic profile, and may apply for authorization to issue electronic invoices (factura electrónica) if it will charge CMRA or scanning fees.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration / Folio Electrónico
Certified copy of the Public Deed
Identification and appointment certificate of the legal representative (Treasurer)
Proof of registered address (lease or registered-agent confirmation)
DGI registration form (Formulario de Inscripción RUC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI queries missing documents, complete and upload the information in the SIF virtual office; where the representative is abroad, grant an additional notarized power to a local representative. Proactive regularization avoids late-filing surcharges under applicable DGI leniency procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating License (Aviso de Operación) and Postal-Intermediary CMRA Notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipalidad de Panamá / relevant District Municipality — Ventanilla Única de Atención al Inversionista; notification to Dirección General de Correos y Telégrafos (Ministerio de Gobierno)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Aviso de Operación / Licencia Comercial e Industrial covering 'servicios de oficina virtual, recepción de correspondencia y escaneo digital' under ISIC 8299 / NAICS 561431. File the municipal application, declare estimated annual gross revenue for tax rating, and pay the municipal aviso tax. Because the activity includes commercial mail receiving, file a complementary notification with the Dirección General de Correos classifying the company as a private mail-intermediary or scanning agent operating under delegated postal services rules, confirming that no reserved postal exclusivity is infringed.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Folio Electrónico registration certificate
Lease agreement or registered-office title
Identity document of legal representative
Aviso de Operación application form and tax declaration
Postal-intermediary notification letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality reclassifies the activity as a regulated or higher-taxed business, submit the corrected ISIC code and postal notification; pay any adjusted municipal fee, and appeal to the municipal tax chamber to lift a suspension; under Vesting Law (Ley de Aviso) the operation may temporarily continue during the appeal if prior taxes are paid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Operational Compliance Clearances — Data Protection, Fire Civil Defense, Occupational Safety, and Environmental Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Autoridad Nacional de Transparencia y Acceso a la Información (ANTAI); Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE); Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because mail scanning involves processing personal data as a digital service, register the corporation as a data controller under Ley 81 de 2019 with ANTAI. Secure the fire-prevention and civil-defense certificate from the Bomberos for the scanning office. Submit the workplace safety registration and ergonomic compliance plan to MITRADEL. Finally, file the environmental registration or low-impact declaration with MiAMBIENTE for the office activities.
required_dossiers: ANTAI data-processing registration form
Fire safety inspection certificate (Cuerpo de Bomberos)
Occupational health & safety plan (MITRADEL)
Environmental registration/commitment form (MiAMBIENTE)
Floor plan of the mail-scanning office
Proof of waste management contract for e-waste and secure paper shredding
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct administrative queries within 10 business days; request extension or transition to the simplified environmental registration where the activity is confirmed low-impact; rectify fire-hazard items identified by the Bomberos and resubmit for re-inspection; missing ANTAI documents may be supplemented electronically.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) and the respective Municipalidad (Ventanilla Única) for commercial operation; Dirección General de Correos y Telégrafos for postal-intermediary oversight
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia Comercial e Industrial / Aviso de Operación (Municipal Operating Notice) combined with the private postal-intermediary CMRA notification and digital-scanning data-processing permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Verificación del Desempeño Ambiental; co-supervised with the Municipality for local discharge permits
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I — Environmental Registration (Registro Ambiental) or exempt declaration for low-impact administrative office activities; no Full EIA Report required for the virtual office and mail-scanning function, provided no hazardous operations are installed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with Decreto Ejecutivo No. 2 de 2009 (BOD, COD, TSS and pH 6–9) and municipal sewer discharge limits; no industrial VOC or point-source combustion emissions are generated by scanning equipment; e-waste handling and disposal must comply with Ley 41 de 2013; shredded paper and confidential scanning residuals must be managed through an authorized recycling or secure-waste disposal contractor with manifest records retained for 5 years.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá fire-safety certification covering the scanning and mail-storage premises; structural load reconnaissance certificate issued by a licensed civil engineer for archives and mail racks; MITRADEL workplace-safety registration, ergonomic clearance for scanning stations, and personnel hygiene protocol for mail handling; additional clearance by the Autoridad de Innovación Gubernamental (AIG) is advisable where cloud scanning services interconnect with public digital infrastructure.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) - portal: SIT (Sistema Integrado de Tributación) at https://dgi.mef.gob.pa/; e-invoicing and RUC management are performed exclusively through the SIT platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporation: execute the public deed of the Sociedad Anónima before a Panamanian notary, appoint a licensed resident agent and officers, and register the deed at the Registro Público de Panamá (no minimum share capital required; non-resident ownership is permitted). Step 2 - Municipal license: obtain the Aviso de Operación from the municipality of the registered fiscal address (for a CMRA/virtual-office business, the municipal commercial license category 'servicios profesionales y de correspondencia'). Step 3 - RUC application: file the DGI RUC registration through the SIT web portal or at the DGI regional office presenting the testified deed copy, the resident-agent certificate, the Aviso de Operación, the certified appointment of the legal representative, passport copies of the foreign officers, and proof of the Panamanian fiscal domicile. Step 4 - Activation: DGI issues the 11-digit RUC (the single tax identifier for income tax, ITBMS, and withholdings) and activates the taxpayer in the ITBMS registrant registry. Step 5 - E-invoicing enrollment: request registration in the facturación electrónica system through SIT, upload the legal representative's electronic signature certificate, and obtain the E-Code issuing credentials. Step 6 - Operations start only after the RUC and e-invoicing activation are confirmed; the Aviso de Operación must also be renewed/validated by the municipality for the fiscal year.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope - the Panamanian S.A. is a tax resident but is taxed only on Panama-source income at the entity level (25% corporate rate); active foreign-source income is exempt under the territorial rule if the operative situs of the activity is outside Panama. No Pass_Through_Eligible status exists for S.A. companies, and the Tax_Exempt_Zone regimes (Colón Free Zone, City of Knowledge SEDE) are not applicable to a domestic virtual-office CMRA operation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Neither US-style check-the-box nor hybrid-mismatch elections exist in Panama. Available statutory elections: (i) classification as Gran Contribuyente (Large Taxpayer) under DGI criteria with large-taxpayer filing obligations; (ii) election to apply the Simplified Income Tax Regime (SIS) with optional IVA promedio (approximate ITBMS) for businesses with gross Panama-source income up to B/.300,000 per year - strategically relevant for a small CMRA S.A.; (iii) board-resolution election designating the company as an export-service provider to evidence the 0% ITBMS export treatment for cross-border mail-scanning services; (iv) election to pay dividends tax through the statutory dividend prepayment mechanism (CUM) rather than upon actual distribution; hybrid-mismatch defenses rely exclusively on evidencing the non-residence of the beneficiary rather than on any elective regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) - Panama's VAT-equivalent imposed on the transfer of movable goods and the provision of services in Panamanian territory (7% standard; 10% hotel/tourism; 3% Colon Free Zone; reduced rates on basic foodstuffs; ISC excise applies separately to liquor, cigarettes, and fuels).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.0.00 (no de minimis exemption): any person or entity regularly transferring goods or rendering services in Panama must register for ITBMS upon the first taxable transaction. A CMRA S.A. generating Panama-source service income must register regardless of volume. Non-resident digital-service platforms were additionally captured by Law 30 of 2022, which established simplified ITBMS registration for foreign suppliers of digital services with a B/.250,000 annual digital-services turnover threshold; this threshold does not apply to a Panamanian-domiciled S.A.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time fiscal clearance model under Law 179 of 2020 and Executive Decree No. 41 of 2022 (as amended). The taxpayer's billing software must transmit each e-invoice XML instance (DGE-XML document standard) via the SIT web-service API (SOAP/REST with mutual TLS authenticated by the PKCS#12 digital certificate of the legal representative) to DGI; DGI validates the document in real time and returns a unique electronic authorization code (E-Code) plus a validation timestamp; only the version containing the E-Code may be delivered to the client and recognized as a fiscal document. A QR code containing the E-Code is embedded in the invoice. Credit notes, debit notes, and export invoices follow the same real-time flow; export invoices must carry the dedicated export-document type in the DGE-XML schema and reference the customs export declaration. The rollout is phased by taxpayer size and became mandatory for all active RUC taxpayers in the 2024-2025 cycle. Sanctions: invoices without a valid E-Code are void for tax-credit and expense-deduction purposes, and the issuer is fined under the Código Fiscal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods (physical departure through customs) and exports of services are zero-rated at 0% ITBMS. A virtual-office/mail-scanning S.A. qualifies for zero-rating when: (a) the recurring subscription and scanning services are contracted by a non-resident client with no Panamanian establishment; (b) the digital files are delivered or made accessible outside Panama (remote platform, overseas data center, foreign e-mail domain of the client); (c) payment for the service remits from abroad; (d) the contract contains a place-of-consumption/place-of-use clause excluding Panama; (e) an export-service declaration is filed with DGI and the export-service contract is registered. Zero-rating is denied, and the service becomes taxable at 7%, where the mail-scanning activity benefits a Panamanian branch, a Panama-domiciled co-working user, or any Panamanian addressee/beneficiary. Panama operates a fully dollarized economy with no central bank and no statutory FX-repatriation obligation; therefore no 180-day inward remittance deadline exists and the structured field is set to 0 days.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación de Mercancías) evidencing physical exit of hard-copy mail or consolidated shipments when physical forwarding is used - filed through the customs electronic single window
Registered Export Services Certificate or notarized export-service contract identifying the non-resident client, service description, fees, and place of consumption outside Panama

Bill of Lading / Master Air Waybill for physical mail-outs, or the digital delivery log showing server-side transmission of scanned data files to the client's offshore platform with IP geolocation records
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT or foreign-bank transfer evidence proving receipt of foreign-currency payment from the non-resident buyer
E-code ITBMS export invoice (DGE-XML export document type) issued through the DGI e-invoicing system
Certificate of non-residency or the foreign tax identification number of the client together with the executed subscription agreement
Internal work-order records demonstrating that the mail-scanning activity took place in Panama but the output was delivered abroad
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI's fiscalization unit (Dirección de Fiscalización) audits export-credit claims with emphasis on sham non-resident clients, intra-group service arrangements, and service consumption by Panamanian beneficiaries. Where zero-rating is disallowed, DGI re-assesses 7% ITBMS on the undeclared revenue plus statutory compensatory interest (currently about 9% per annum) and fines: (i) up to 100% of omitted ITBMS for false E-code e-invoice declarations; (ii) RUC and e-invoicing authorization suspension for repeat violations; (iii) criminal liability under the tax-crime provisions of the Código Fiscal and Ley No. 8 de 2010 - three to six years imprisonment and fines of B/.10,000 to B/.100,000 for export documentation containing falsified customs data. Any ITBMS export credit refunded as 'Saldo a Favor' (offset against future taxes or paid out by DGI) is clawed back with interest, and the taxpayer is barred from generating export e-invoices for 12 months. Automatic fraud-review red flags include export invoices exceeding 120% of declared export revenue, recurrent invoice cancellations after E-code issuance, and client addresses matching Panamanian or regional mail-forwarding clusters (classic CMRA fraud indicators).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Pago del Impuesto Anual de Franquicia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Republic of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 March of each calendar year; newly incorporated S.A.s pay the first fee at formation and thereafter every 15 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a surcharge plus monthly interest; prolonged delinquency suspends the certificate of good standing and may lead to administrative strike-off of the corporate registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Declaration (Declaración Jurada de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), taxpayer portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March following the 31 December fiscal year close; dormant S.A.s not registered with DGI are not required to file, but must file immediately if DGI issues a registration notice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file when liable exposes the entity to fines of up to USD 1,000 plus interest on any assessed tax; persistent non-compliance can trigger a tax deficiency assessment and collection action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial-Ownership Confirmation (Declaración Jurada de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Resident agent / Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) Beneficial-Ownership Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days of the incorporation anniversary and within 30 days of any shareholding change; exact DGI portal filing is required for entities holding a DGI beneficial-ownership account.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance blocks the issuance of a good-standing certificate and may subject the entity and its resident agent to administrative penalties under Panama's Law 23 of 2015.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit mandatory for public-interest entities and regulated industries (banking, securities, insurance, finance, gaming) and for any S.A. with Panama-source gross annual revenue exceeding USD 1,000,000 or total assets exceeding USD 5,000,000; DGI large-taxpayer designation also triggers an audited financial-statement requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the Junta Técnica de Contabilidad (Panama Technical Accounting Board); IFRS for SMEs permitted for non-public-interest entities meeting size exemptions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No public share-register annual return is filed; the resident agent must maintain a confidential beneficial-ownership register and annually obtain a sworn confirmation from the directors/officers confirming the current ownership structure and reporting any transfer or change; changes are logged in the share register and, where applicable, reported to the DGI beneficiary-owner system within 30 days.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–700 per year for a Panama resident agent and registered office; USD 100–250 for virtual mail/scanning continuation
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–8,500 per audit engagement if an audit becomes mandatory or is contractually required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat on net taxable income (unified rate introduced by Law 77 of 2019; previously progressive scale up to 30%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory holiday applies to ISIC 8299 CMRA/digital-scanning activity. Panama applies territorial taxation, so only Panama-source income is within the ISR base. The Cálculo Alterno del Impuesto sobre la Renta (CAIR) operates as a minimum-tax floor computed on taxable costs and expenses, ensuring that the final effective payment cannot fall below the alternative levy.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 101 – Declaración de Renta de Personas Jurídicas, filed through the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) 'Renta en Línea' electronic system (www.dgi.gob.pa).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (plus quarterly estimated advance payments due in March, June, September and December).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three (3) months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year companies the deadline is March 31 of the following tax period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Stated fiscal year or fiscal period end date (e.g., 31/12/2024).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The filing entity is the Panamanian S.A.; a non-resident shareholder does not complete this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 15-digit Registro Único del Contribuyente tax identification number assigned by the DGI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The company must register for a RUC through a Panamanian legal representative before any filing is accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All Panama-source gross revenue, including virtual-office rental, mail receipt, scanning and related administrative service fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue generated by activities physically performed in Panama is taxable; foreign-source income should be excluded and evidenced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income derived exclusively from sources outside Panama (territorial exemption) and other expressly exempt receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxpayer bears the burden of proof; documentary evidence of the foreign source must be retained and produced on DGI request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary and necessary operating expenses: office lease, utility bills, employee wages, equipment depreciation, software and scanning consumables.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Charges from foreign related parties must be arm's-length and supported by documentation; undocumented payments are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross taxable income minus deductible costs and expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Negative balances are available as losses and may be carried forward for a maximum of five (5) fiscal years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax determined by applying the 25% statutory rate to net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the CAIR alternative calculation produces a higher amount, the excess must be added in the appropriate supplementary field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for quarterly advances prepaid during the year, plus any withholding taxes borne by the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Advances are not refundable; any surplus credit carries forward to the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 – Saldo a Pagar o Crédito a Favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due after credits, or the excess credit available for carry-forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The balance must be paid in Balboas (pegged 1:1 to the US Dollar) via the DGI's electronic banking channels.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Untimely filing: late-filing surcharge of 10% of the tax due, plus daily interest (approximately 1% per month). Administrative fines for non-filing range between USD/PAB 100 and USD/PAB 500. Fraudulent filing: criminal prosecution for tax evasion, restitution, fines and imprisonment from 2 to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid from profits already subject to Panamanian ISR; 20% on dividends distributed out of non-taxed or exempt profits (e.g., offshore income not subject to ISR in Panama).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must obtain an official Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) in the treaty jurisdiction and deliver it, together with a DGI-filed application for treaty benefits and a declaration of beneficial ownership, to the Panamanian withholding agent before distribution. The withholding agent applies the reduced rate (Panama's DTAs typically provide 5%-15% for dividends) or the non-resident shareholder submits a refund claim to the DGI for any excess WHT. Active DTAs include those with Korea, Mexico, Singapore, France, Portugal, Spain, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Italy, Ireland, the UK, the UAE and Barbados.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and technical-assistance payments made to non-residents for industrial, commercial or scientific know-how used in Panama are subject to a 12.5% statutory WHT on gross payments. Interest paid to foreign lenders is generally outside Panamanian WHT where the lender has no Panamanian permanent establishment, but related-party financing must satisfy transfer-pricing rules. Treaty-protocol rates for royalties and interest typically range from 5% to 10% when a DTA applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD/PAB 6,000,000 in aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions for mandatory preparation of the TP Local File and Master File (Law 54 of 2017, as regulated by Executive Decree 486/2019). Taxpayers below the threshold must nevertheless substantiate arm's-length pricing for all related-party dealings.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Law 70 of 2019 and Executive Decree 351/2019 impose Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) on companies tax-resident in Panama that perform 'relevant activities,' including distribution and service centers. A CMRA/virtual-office entity that receives and scans mail in Panama qualifies as a service-center activity and must demonstrate, on an annual ESR declaration filed with the DGI, adequate physical premises, qualified full-time staff, operational expenditure and management located in Panama. An S.A. operating on paper only, without actual execution of the CMRA activity in Panama, fails the substance test and may forfeit its tax-residence status.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting Panama-source CMRA revenue from Formulario 101 or inflating deductions by creating false invoices for rent, payroll or subcontracted scanning services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Compulsory restitution of the evaded ISR, late-payment interest at approximately 1% monthly, a late-filing/adjustment surcharge of up to 10% of the tax, and monetary fines of up to ten times the evaded tax. Criminal prosecution under the Panamanian Penal Code and Tax Code carries imprisonment of 2 to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers signing false returns may be indicted as co-perpetrators, face preventive embargoes of personal assets, travel bans, disqualification from holding corporate office, and civil restitution obligations when the corporate vehicle is used as a façade.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the S.A. as a letterbox with no physical office, no employees, no corporate records in Panama, and no actual execution of the declared commercial-mail-receiving and scanning activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of up to USD/PAB 50,000 for ESR non-compliance, denial or withdrawal of the tax-residence certificate by the DGI, disclosure to the EU/OECD under harmful-tax-practices frameworks, and possible strike-off or forced liquidation through the Registro Público.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be disqualified from acting as officers of any Panamanian company, held civilly liable to the State for penalties, subjected to cross-border travel restrictions, and criminally charged if the shell structure was used to conceal beneficial ownership.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the virtual-office and mail-scanning platform, together with the corporate bank account, to receive or layer proceeds of fraud, drug trafficking or organized crime disguised as routine service fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal liability under Law 23 of 2015 and Penal Code Article 254: imprisonment of 5 to 12 years, corporate fines, confiscation of proceeds and instrumentalities, and reporting to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF). Aggravated circumstances raise penalties to 10 to 15 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who execute, conceal or benefit from the laundering scheme face extended imprisonment, asset freezes and forfeiture, travel bans, debarment from financial-sector positions, and joint and several civil liability for the illicit proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging below-market administrative or scanning fees to a foreign parent or related group so that the Panamanian CMRA entity reports artificial losses, or making undocumented management/royalty payments offshore to erode Panama-source taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI recharacterization at arm's length, additional ISR at 25% on the upward adjustment, monthly interest at approximately 1%, penalties on the omitted tax (with enhanced fines in fraud cases), and mandatory CAIR reconciliation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign defective TP documentation may be jointly liable for the adjusted tax, interest and penalties, and face criminal tax-evasion charges if the mispricing is shown to be intentional.
